description:
SHIPPED s470bn (Opus, 2026-09-05), commit `00b26f8`.

`for my $x (@a, @b)` lowered to `(p-foreach-raw ($x (p-flatten-args (list @a
@b))))`, which builds a fresh vector of every element before the first
iteration.  On feread2 (2 x 500 elements, 30k repeats) the flattening is 88 % of
the row.

THE LICENCE NEEDS NO NEW FACT: `p-foreach-raw` already requires the loop
variable to be READ-ONLY (#862 ARM A) and every array named in the list to
neither escape nor be written in the body (#1140).  `foreach-arrays` adds only
the list SHAPE test (`Pl::Parser::_foreach_bare_arrays`: two or more elements,
each ONE PPI::Token::Symbol with the `@` sigil, a plain word name, no subscript).
The comma splitter is now ONE function shared with `_foreach_scalar_elements`.

IT SNAPSHOTS what the flattener snapshots: each source's ELEMENT-STORAGE vector
and length, once, at loop entry (%p-make-array-run) â so a push during the loop
does not extend the iteration, which is today's multi-array behaviour.
%p-run-elt-raw finds the source by scanning the cumulative ends (1-2 fixnum
compares for two or three arrays).  ONE expander still: %expand-foreach takes
the run through the same three slots `rawp` parameterises.

=== DONE (s470bn) ===
Ceiling -88.3 % (control -2.6 %); SHIPPED -78.3 % (0.5702 -> 0.1235 s at
N=30 000, control -1.9 %).  `tools/bench-exec.pl` gains `feread3` (the same 1000
elements over THREE arrays) as the scaling control.

THE FINDING FOR THE NEXT ROUND: the shape occurs in NONE of the 1035 files of
the four populations.  corpus-diff and the wide emission A/B show ZERO `:arrays`
sites in perl-tests, perl's own t/, the CPAN board and lib/; a grep finds four
`for my $x (@a, @b)` spellings across all of them and every one declines (the
perl-tests/for.t case writes the loop variable, which is the licence working).
So the win is real and the row is real, but whether real programs hit it is a
question for the macro rows.
subject: foreach-arrays: `for my $x (@a, @b)` iterates each array in turn, no flattened temporary (feread2 -78 %) - but the shape occurs in ZERO corpus files
